title: Read Malory properly
blurb: The whole of Le Morte d'Arthur: 21 books, 502 chapters, about 336,000 words. Roughly a month at a chapter or two a day.
note: The reader keeps your place by chapter, glosses the hard words as you meet them, and marks the passages the research ledger validates. Book X (Tristram) is 88 chapters and is where most readers stop — it is fine to skip it and come back.

stops.note: Start with Caxton's preface. He explains, in 1485, exactly why he is printing this and what he expects a reader to get from it.
Book XIII, if you want the Grail quest on its own.
Book XVIII, if you want the fall on its own.
